name: OSV.dev (Open Source Vulnerabilities API)
operator: Google (OSV.dev, open-source vulnerability database and API)
tier_rationale: Established company with published terms, a privacy policy and a business offering (A8 trusted); P185 cond 5 'Registry providers osv (Google) and github: tier trusted'.

reliability.justification: Aggregates the advisories of the ecosystem databases (GitHub Advisory Database, PyPA, Go, RustSec, Debian, Ubuntu...) in one schema; ranges are as precise as each upstream database.

vulns.title: OSV API GET /v1/vulns/{id} (CVE, GHSA and the derived DEBIAN-CVE/UBUNTU-CVE distro records)

terms.quote: Sources: OSV (CC BY 4.0, per-source licences, attribution) 'open'; GHSA through the GitHub REST API 'key-terms' (as P111).

vulns.notes: Quote: binding council text (P185 cond 2); research C0437 'OSV data CC-BY 4.0 (per-source licenses)', verified live 2026-11-26 (200 in 0.06-0.15 s, no rate-limit headers, no key). An unknown id answers 404 {"code":5,"message":"Vulnerability not found"} (documented absence, also for the DEBIAN-CVE/UBUNTU-CVE ids of CVEs without a distro record). /v1/query and /v1/querybatch (package@version) are never built until a purl/package entity type exists (P185 cond 3: package queries would disclose the internal software inventory). Attribution: OSV.dev, CC BY 4.0 (per-source licences).

notes: Owned by batch p2-G08-1 (P185 osv_ghsa). Other batches extend it (osv__<suffix>.json). No published quota ('no key, generous'): min_interval 0.5 s and the CVE fan-out rule (P183 cond 3) keep the per-case load small.
